answer: The consequences of Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) include the ability for remote attackers to execute scripts in the user's browser, which can bypass existing security controls. This type of attack is particularly insidious because it is difficult for end users to detect. Attackers can exploit vulnerabilities in user-generated content sites, such as bulletin boards or blogs, to inject malicious scripts that affect other users [Source 1][Source 2].

## Consequences

controls in place, but if a remote attacker is allowed to execute scripts (through injecting them in to user-generated content like bulletin boards) then these controls may be bypassed. Further, these attacks are very difficult for an end user to detect.
